canonical_name: TinySTM -- a lightweight word-based software transactional memory (Felber, Fetzer, Riegel, Marlier; 2007-)
lineage: Software transactional memory (Shavit & Touitou 1995) as the research lineage that competed with lock-based concurrency in the multicore decade: TinySTM (2007, Univ. Neuchatel / TU Dresden) uses time-based validation (Riegel), encounter- or commit-time locking, and ships micro-benchmarks (bank, intset) that count aborts/commits. The human record: STM lost the mainstream to fine-grained locks and lock-free structures, survived in Haskell/Clojure and Intel TSX -- a partly SUPERSEDED design, preserved.
version: github.com/patrickmarlier/tinystm master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes; 1.0.5 lineage)
entry_points: stm_init / stm_start / stm_load / stm_store / stm_commit; test/bank/bank (accounts transferring under contention)

example.input: 4 threads transferring between 256 accounts for 2 s
example.output: commits, aborts, and the invariant: total balance unchanged

upstream_docs: Felber, Fetzer, Riegel, Dynamic Performance Tuning of Word-Based Software Transactional Memory, PPoPP 2008
Riegel, Felber, Fetzer, A Lazy Snapshot Algorithm with Eager Validation, DISC 2006

human_capability_summary.built_to: let threads compose memory operations into atomic transactions that abort and retry on conflict instead of holding locks
human_capability_summary.pressure: contention (conflicting transactions abort), memory reordering, the cost of validation
human_capability_summary.success_means: the bank's total balance is invariant under any interleaving; aborts are bounded and retried

known_human_problem_solved: composable atomic memory updates without locks
human_environmental_pressure: resource contention, competing writers, retry cost
human_failure_condition: abort storms under high contention (livelock-like) or a validation bug that commits a conflicting transaction
behavioral_entry_point: shrink the number of accounts (-a 8) with many threads to drive the abort rate up; switch the locking design flags in Makefile.common

lineage_relations.note: rival answers to multicore synchronization: transactions vs lock-free + backoff

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run tinystm-marlier
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: let threads compose memory operations into atomic transactions that abort and retry on conflict instead of holding locks
